title: Ordinals: order types, successors, and limits
summary: Names for well-order types, their comparison, and the difference between successors and limits.
abstract: The natural numbers, the natural numbers followed by one last point, and two consecutive copies of the natural numbers all have the same countable size. Their orders are different, and ordinals distinguish those differences. Every well-order has exactly one ordinal as its order type: two well-ordered sets have the same ordinal precisely when a bijection preserves their order. Successor ordinals have a last point, while nonzero limit ordinals have none. The least upper bound of any set of ordinals is their union, providing a precise limit for a sequence of increasing stages.
